description: Comprehensive reasoning vault for complex numbers, imaginary unit powers, square roots of negative numbers, addition, subtraction, multiplication, conjugates, division, modulus, and AC circuit impedance synthesis; synthesis 2026-11-20 added powers-of-i cycles, conjugate equations, real/purely-imaginary conditions and periodic powers; the Thai past-paper round 2026-11-21 confirmed multi-relation conjugate and axis-condition forms (exam-style choice and numeric-response distractors).

archetypes.name: Imaginary Unit Definition and Fundamental Identity
archetypes.coreConcept: The imaginary unit i satisfies i^2 = -1, allowing evaluation of expressions with negative square roots.
archetypes.mentalModel: Quarter-turn 90-degree phase rotation on the complex Argand plane.
archetypes.figureNone: Complex-number algebra in standard form; the work is symbolic.

archetypes.name: Square Roots of Negative Real Numbers
archetypes.coreConcept: Express square roots of negative numbers as pure imaginary numbers: sqrt(-n) = i*sqrt(n) for n > 0.
archetypes.mentalModel: Factoring out the negative unit as imaginary dimension.
archetypes.figureNone: Complex-number algebra in standard form; the work is symbolic.

archetypes.name: Addition of Complex Numbers in Standard Form
archetypes.coreConcept: Combine real parts with real parts and imaginary parts with imaginary parts: (a+bi) + (c+di) = (a+c) + (b+d)i.
archetypes.mentalModel: Two-dimensional vector addition of orthogonal components.

archetypes.name: Subtraction of Complex Numbers via Component Difference
archetypes.coreConcept: Distribute negative sign across both real and imaginary terms: (a+bi) - (c+di) = (a-c) + (b-d)i.
archetypes.mentalModel: Reversing the subtrahend vector before vector addition.

archetypes.name: Multiplying Pure Imaginary Numbers
archetypes.coreConcept: Product of pure imaginary numbers yields a real number using i^2 = -1: (bi)(di) = -bd.
archetypes.mentalModel: Two consecutive 90-degree rotations resulting in a 180-degree reflection into the negative real line.
archetypes.figureNone: Complex-number algebra in standard form; the work is symbolic.

archetypes.name: Multiplying Complex Numbers via FOIL Expansion
archetypes.coreConcept: Expand four terms and simplify i^2 = -1 to separate into real and imaginary parts: (a+bi)(c+di) = (ac-bd) + (ad+bc)i. L3 problem form: show a worked solution that makes the mistake 'positive last term (tag `t02-c01-u01-positive-last-term-trap`)'; the prompt shows the work as 'Line N: $...$' lines and the learner picks the first wrong line (answerSpec `choice` with `verify.flaw`; asking for the corrected value lets the learner just recompute, 06 §2.3).
archetypes.mentalModel: Combined rotational scaling of complex vectors.
archetypes.figureNone: Complex-number algebra in standard form; the work is symbolic.
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.4; cores: smartmathpro, tyler-wallace-algebra
archetypes.levelNote: Cubes or products of three binomials are in scope; trap i-cubed-in-cubed-binomial = i^3 taken as +i inside the binomial-cube expansion (distinct from misreading the remainder cycle).

archetypes.name: Complex Conjugates and Modulus Product
archetypes.coreConcept: Multiplying a complex number by its conjugate eliminates imaginary part: (a+bi)(a-bi) = a^2 + b^2 = |z|^2. L3 problem form: show a worked solution that makes the mistake 'difference of squares minus sign (tag `t02-c01-u01-difference-of-squares-minus-sign-trap`)'; the prompt shows the work as 'Line N: $...$' lines and the learner picks the first wrong line (answerSpec `choice` with `verify.flaw`; asking for the corrected value lets the learner just recompute, 06 §2.3).
archetypes.mentalModel: Reflecting across real axis to create pure real magnitude squared.
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.4; cores: smartmathpro, mathematics-vision-project, thai-exams
archetypes.levelNote: For compact magnitude expressions that conceal a perfect-square identity, identify and factor the square before evaluating the magnitude. Thai exam numeric-response items can require this structural recognition without providing distractor choices. When a solved value feeds a follow-up magnitude or conjugate product, keep the nonnegative sum-of-squares identity intact.

archetypes.name: Dividing Complex Numbers via Denominator Conjugate Rationalization
archetypes.coreConcept: Multiply numerator and denominator by denominator conjugate to make denominator real: (a+bi)/(c+di) = ((a+bi)(c-di))/(c^2+d^2). L3 problem form: show a worked solution that makes the mistake 'divide real and imag parts directly (tag `t02-c01-u01-divide-real-and-imag-parts-directly-trap`)'; the prompt shows the work as 'Line N: $...$' lines and the learner picks the first wrong line (answerSpec `choice` with `verify.flaw`; asking for the corrected value lets the learner just recompute, 06 §2.3).
archetypes.mentalModel: Normalizing complex ratios to a common real denominator scale.
archetypes.figureNone: Complex-number algebra in standard form; the work is symbolic.
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.4; cores: smartmathpro, libretexts-math, tyler-wallace-algebra
archetypes.levelNote: Reverse form in scope: given 1/z, find z (the reciprocal of a+bi is its conjugate over a^2+b^2); trap reciprocal-parts-inverted = taking 1/a + (1/b)i.

archetypes.name: AC Series Impedance: Reactance from a Target Magnitude
archetypes.coreConcept: In a series AC circuit Z = R + i(X_L - X_C). Given R, X_C and a target |Z|, find every inductive reactance X_L that achieves it: |Z|^2 = R^2 + X^2 gives X = ±sqrt(|Z|^2 - R^2), and each sign gives a different X_L, which must be checked to be positive.
archetypes.mentalModel: Phasor impedance triangle solved backwards, with both signs of the reactance considered.
archetypes.governingRelation: X = \pm\sqrt{|Z|^2 - R^2},\quad X_L = X_C + X,\ X_L > 0
archetypes.figureNone: Complex-number algebra in standard form; the work is symbolic.

archetypes.name: Quadratic Parameter from Complex-Root Conditions
archetypes.coreConcept: For x^2 + bx + k = 0 with real b given, find the real k for which the roots are non-real and have a given modulus. The discriminant condition b^2 - 4k < 0 bounds k, the conjugate pair has product |z|^2 = k, and the roots then follow from the quadratic formula.
archetypes.mentalModel: Discriminant condition plus conjugate-pair product fix the parameter.
archetypes.figureNone: Complex-number algebra in standard form; the work is symbolic.

archetypes.name: Powers of i Beyond the First Cycle
archetypes.coreConcept: Any integer power of i (large, negative, or given by an expression) reduces through the period-4 cycle i, -1, -i, 1; sums of four consecutive powers cancel. L2 asks for a single structured power or a short sum; L3 asks which exponents (from a set or range) make a sum or product take a stated value, so the solver must test the residues mod 4 case by case.
archetypes.mentalModel: A four-hour clock: only the exponent's remainder mod 4 matters, and a full lap of four consecutive powers adds to zero.
archetypes.figureNone: Pure exponent arithmetic on i; a plane figure would not add information at this level.
archetypes.levelNote: L2: one structured exponent (negative, or built from a product/factorial/sum) or a short sum. L3 only when the solver must count or choose exponents and reject the residues that fail the stated value (check=edge, listed in blindSolve.edgeRejected) or pick the method (strategy=choose). A single large exponent is L1-L2, never L3.
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.4; cores: smartmathpro, tyler-wallace-algebra

archetypes.name: Equations in z and Its Conjugate by Equating Parts
archetypes.coreConcept: An equation that mixes z and its conjugate is solved by writing z = a + bi, collecting real and imaginary parts on each side, and equating them to get two real equations. L2: linear in z and its conjugate. L3: includes the product of z and its conjugate (a^2 + b^2) or asks for a derived quantity of the solution.
archetypes.mentalModel: One complex equation is two real equations stacked together: the real line and the imaginary line must both balance.
archetypes.governingRelation: z = a + bi,\ \bar{z} = a - bi \land (p + qi = r + si \iff p = r \land q = s)
archetypes.figureNone: Symbolic equation solving; the answer is a single complex number.
archetypes.levelNote: L2 for a linear equation in z and its conjugate, including a derived follow-up quantity of the solution (one more step stays L2). L3 only when the z times conjugate term produces two candidates and one is ruled out by a stated condition (check=edge with edgeRejected), or two conditions must be combined (setup=model). Reverse form: give the solution and ask for a coefficient. Thai PAT 1 items confirm a common L3 extension: solve both component equations, then simplify a requested conjugate-based invariant; choice distractors can omit one component relation or stop before the derived quantity.
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.4; cores: smartmathpro

archetypes.name: Parameter Conditions for a Real or Purely Imaginary Result
archetypes.coreConcept: Choose a real parameter so that a product or quotient of complex numbers is real (imaginary part zero) or purely imaginary (real part zero and imaginary part nonzero). The solver must simplify to standard form first, then set the correct part to zero and check the other part is not also zero.
archetypes.mentalModel: Simplify, then look at the two coordinates: 'real' means the point sits on the real axis, 'purely imaginary' means it sits on the imaginary axis but not at the origin.
archetypes.governingRelation: w = X + Yi:\ w \in \mathbb{R} \iff Y = 0;\ w \text{ purely imaginary} \iff X = 0 \land Y \neq 0
archetypes.figureNone: The condition is algebraic on the simplified parts; a figure would show the answer.
archetypes.levelNote: Earns L3 only with check=edge: the nonzero check (purely imaginary needs Y != 0) rejects at least one candidate parameter, recorded in blindSolve.edgeRejected. Rationalising first is extra steps (L2) unless it forces a method choice. Applying the condition to an already simplified a + bi is L2. Thai PAT 1 items also combine real and purely-imaginary conditions on different expressions before asking for a conjugate product; distractors can swap the vanishing components or misuse the norm identity.
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.4; cores: smartmathpro

archetypes.name: Periodic Powers of a Simple Complex Number
archetypes.coreConcept: Some complex numbers reduce to a simple power of i after one or two steps: a quotient of conjugate binomials gives i or -i, and the square of a binomial with equal parts gives an integer times i. Reduce the base first, keep any integer scale factor, then use the period of the reduced base to find the least exponent giving a stated value or a far term of a repeating sequence.
archetypes.mentalModel: Shrink the base to something you know cycles, then let the cycle do the work instead of expanding a huge power.
archetypes.figureNone: Algebraic reduction and periodicity; no figure needed at this level.
archetypes.levelNote: Base L2 (reduce, then use the cycle on an obviously reducible base). L3 when the base is not obviously reducible so the solver must choose the reduction (strategy=choose), or a recurrence start index / rejected exponents give check=edge. Allowed bases reduce to +-i, -1 or k*i^m with integer k (conjugate quotients, squares of binomials with equal parts); no sqrt(2)-normalised bases, no modulus or polar form (later unit). Ask for a result 'equal to 1' or 'real', never 'unit'. Derive assume-period-four from a base of period 2 (a quotient reducing to -1) or a recurrence.
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.4; cores: smartmathpro, tyler-wallace-algebra

archetypes.name: Mixed Operations on Complex Expressions
archetypes.coreConcept: Simplify a single given complex expression that chains two or more taught unit operations in sequence—such as reducing powers of i, expanding binomial products, rationalising quotients by the denominator conjugate, and combining standard-form parts—until the final result is in a + bi form.
archetypes.mentalModel: Treat a compound complex expression as a staged pipeline: resolve inner powers and products or quotients into a + bi first, carry signs cleanly between stages, and combine real and imaginary parts only after each sub-expression is in standard form.
archetypes.governingRelation: i^2 = -1,\ i^{n} = i^{n \bmod 4},\ (a + bi)(c + di) = (ac - bd) + (ad + bc)i,\ \frac{a + bi}{c + di} = \frac{(a + bi)(c - di)}{c^2 + d^2}

cognitiveTraps.description: Applies chained operations out of precedence order (for example, adding a trailing term before completing a product or quotient, or inverting a sum term-by-term before combining the denominator).
Drops or flips a negative sign produced by an earlier step when substituting that intermediate result into the next operation.
Combines a real term directly with an imaginary coefficient into a single term instead of keeping real and imaginary components separate.
Replaces i + i with i^2 = -1 instead of 2i when adding imaginary parts.
Subtracts only the real part of a grouped complex sub-expression and leaves the imaginary sign unchanged.
Treats i^2 as +1 instead of -1 when expanding a binomial product inside the chain.
Drops the middle cross terms when squaring or multiplying complex binomials.
Uses the wrong conjugate sign or subtracts squares in the denominator while rationalising a quotient.
Divides real and imaginary components separately instead of multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate.
Maps the exponent remainder modulo 4 to the wrong element of the i-power cycle.
Evaluates a negative exponent of i as if it had the same sign as the positive exponent.
Replaces i^2 with +1 during multi-factor expansion.
Multiplies by the un-conjugated denominator or flips the wrong sign when rationalising a quotient.

archetypes.figureNone: Purely symbolic multi-step complex-number simplification in standard a + bi form; a complex-plane plot does not clarify the algebraic operation sequence.
archetypes.levelNote: Base L2: given expression, obvious execution order, >= 4 real single-transformation steps chaining at least two taught operations in sequence. Earns L3 only when a genuine choice among taught methods is needed (strategy=choose)—for example, spotting a conjugate pair so a product collapses to a real number (a+bi)(a-bi)=a^2+b^2 instead of expanding by FOIL, combining two quotients over a common real denominator when their denominators are conjugates instead of rationalising each fraction separately, or factoring a difference-of-squares structure before expanding. The L3 item must also offer a longer direct route that works, and the blind solver must tag strategy=choose itself (never relabel). Do not use find-the-flaw (diagnose) here; flaw diagnosis stays in the existing L3 single-operation archetypes. Scope boundaries: stay strictly in standard-form arithmetic with integer/rational parts; no sqrt-normalised bases, no modulus or polar form (later unit); do not overlap t02-c01-u01-power-periodicity (periodic bases such as (1+i)^k or conjugate-binomial quotients raised to large powers belong there).
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.4; cores: smartmathpro
